summary: On Shionoya was a sinologist who studied at Tokyo Imperial University (~1899–1902) and the University of Leipzig (~1906–1908). He held a post at Tokyo Imperial University from circa 1920 to 1939.
Orgyen Jikdral Chöying Dorjé studied under Jamgön Kongtrül Lodrö Thaye and Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso. He also taught Shechen Gyaltsab.
Orgyen Tendzin Norbu studied under Patrul Rinpoche and Jamyang Khyentse Wangpo. He later taught Shenphen Nangwa.

Tibetologist and Buddhist studies scholar Orna Almogi studied at Ngagyur Nyingma Institute and under Khenpo Wangchuk Sonam, David P. Jackson, and Lambert Schmithausen. She has held posts at the Nepal-German Manuscript Preservation Project, University of Hamburg, and International Institute for Buddhist Studies.

Osamu Hayashima, a scholar of Buddhist studies, philosophy, and Indology, studied under Noritoshi Aramaki and at the University of Hamburg (1992). He held posts at Nagasaki University, Shiga University of Medical Science, and Ryukoku University.
Osamu Izumoji is a scholar in the fields of Buddhist studies and Japanology. He has held academic posts at Kyoto Prefectural University and Ryukoku University.

Osamu Oba was a scholar of sinology and history/archaeology who studied at Kansai University. He held posts at Kansai University (~1968–1998), Kogakkan University (~1998–2002), and the University of the Sacred Heart.

Osamu Takata was a scholar of Buddhist studies and history/archaeology who studied under Baiei Henmi. He held positions at Tohoku University (attested 1961) and as head of the art department at Tokyo National Research Institute for Cultural Properties (attested 1967).

Linguist Osborn Bergin studied at University College Cork, the School of Irish Learning under Kuno Meyer, and the University of Freiburg under Heinrich Zimmer. He held posts at University College Dublin (~1909–1940) and Dublin Institute for Advanced Studies (~1940).

Indologist, Buddhist studies scholar, and linguist Oskar von Hinüber studied at Mainz, Tübingen, and Erlangen-Nuremberg, and under Paul Thieme. He held positions at Mainz (1965–1981) and Freiburg (Chair in Indic Studies, 1981–2006), and directed the Nepal Research Centre.

Osmund Bopearachchi studied at the University of Kelaniya, CNRS, Panthéon-Sorbonne University, and Paris-Sorbonne University. He served as Emeritus Director at CNRS (1989) and as Adjunct Professor at the University of California, Berkeley (~2014).

Osvald Sirén, a scholar of sinology and history/archaeology, completed his doctoral studies at the University of Helsinki. He held posts at Stockholm University (1908–1923), Harvard and Yale (1916–1917), the Guimet Museum (1924–1925), and Nationalmuseum (1926–1945).

Indologist Othmar Frank studied at the universities of Paris and London. He held teaching posts at Kaiser-Heinrich-Gymnasium Bamberg, Banz Abbey, and served as professor at the universities of Bamberg, Würzburg (from 1821), and Munich (from 1826).
Indologist Otoya Tanaka studied at the University of Tokyo under Naoshiro Tsuji (~1926–1930). He later held a professorship at Chuo University from circa 1957 to 1974.
Otto Blau studied at Martin Luther University of Halle-Wittenberg in 1848, under August Friedrich Pott (~1848–1851), and at the University of Leipzig (~1850–1852).

Otto Fischer was a scholar of sinology, Japanology, and history/archaeology who studied at Tübingen, Munich, Vienna, and Göttingen. He served as director of the Staatsgalerie Stuttgart (1920) and Kunstmuseum Basel (1927), and taught at the University of Basel (~1927–1937).

Sinologist and Indologist Otto Franke studied at Freiburg, Göttingen, and under Wilhelm Grube. He held the inaugural chair of Chinese Language and Culture at Hamburg/Hamburgisches Kolonialinstitut (1910–1923) and was Professor of Sinology at Humboldt University of Berlin (1923–1931).

Linguist and religious studies scholar Otto Höfler studied at the University of Vienna under Rudolf Much, as well as at Lund and Kiel. He held professorships at Kiel (1935), Munich (1938–1945, 1954), and Vienna (1957–1971).

Otto Jahn, a scholar of history, archaeology, and linguistics, studied at Kiel, Leipzig, and Humboldt University of Berlin. He held academic posts at the universities of Kiel (~1839–1845), Greifswald (~1842–1847), Leipzig (~1847–1851), and Bonn (~1855–1869).

Otto Maenchen-Helfen was a scholar of sinology, Central Asian studies, and history/archaeology. He studied at Vienna, Gothenburg, and Leipzig under August Conrady, and held posts at the Marx-Engels-Lenin Institute (1927–1929), Mills College (1939–1947), and UC Berkeley (1947–1962).
